meta.title: Khmer B1 Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1000 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Khmer is the language of Cambodia. Both study directions in one deck: Khmer → English (see the Khmer, recall the meaning) and English → Khmer (see an English meaning, recall the Khmer). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1000 words for an intermediate learner, aligned to B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main points of clear standard input on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure, etc.' — a learner here is able to deal with most situations likely to arise while travelling, to produce simple connected text on familiar topics, and to describe experiences and events, dreams, hopes and ambitions, and briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Khmer, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 156 of the 1000 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — work and careers, money, banking and the economy, education, the news, media and technology, government, law and society, the environment, health and medicine, travel and accommodation, the household, relationships and the stages of life, feelings and character, religion, Buddhism and Cambodian custom, the nouns for ideas, reasons and plans, the connectors that join sentences, and the verbs of thinking, deciding and changing — and the other 844 are the commonest remaining words of Khmer, counted in the articles of the Khmer Wikipedia. The first day's greetings come first and the rest are dealt by that count, so the words you meet most often come early; an encyclopaedia's commonest words lean towards the written language. Every headword is printed in Khmer script with Wiktionary's romanisation beneath it, a phonetic spelling that shows the vowel each letter's series gives it (ក with ា is kaa, គ with ា is kiə) — the Khmer Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script and the two series. There are no forms to learn: Khmer words never change shape. Real example sentences come with 210 of the 1000 words, three apiece for 33 of them — the sources hold few Khmer sentences — with the word picked out in colour. There is no speaker button, since few devices have a Khmer voice. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, romanisation and some example sentences: English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0), via the kaikki.org extraction and the entries' own pages. Frequency: the Khmer Wikipedia, the dump of 1 November 2026 (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
